title: 127. Quantitative Relationships & Measurement: Cancellation of Units in Calculations
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the correct unit of distance after multiplying speed by time.
questions.question: A car travels at a constant speed of \(15\text{ m/s}\) for \(8\text{ s}\). Which calculation gives the distance traveled, including correct unit cancellation?
questions.explanation: Speed multiplied by time gives distance: \(\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}}\times \text{s}=\text{m}\). The seconds cancel, leaving metres. Then \(15\times 8=120\), so the distance is \(120\text{ m}\). Option A incorrectly leaves the time unit.
questions.hint: Write the units beside every factor before simplifying.

questions.learningObjective: Combine physical units correctly in a force-distance product.
questions.question: A force of \(20\text{ N}\) moves an object \(3\text{ m}\) in the direction of the force. What is the work done, with the correct product unit?
questions.explanation: Work is force times displacement, so \(20\times 3=60\) with product unit \(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}\). The alternative keeps the correct numerical product but divides the unit symbols, giving \(\text{N/m}\) instead of the work unit.
questions.hint: Decide whether the formula multiplies or divides the quantities, then combine the units the same way.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the correct unit of mass after multiplying density by volume.
questions.question: A substance has density \(2\text{ kg/m}^3\) and volume \(5\text{ m}^3\). What is its mass, with units cancelled correctly?
questions.explanation: Density multiplied by volume gives mass: \(\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{m}^3}\times \text{m}^3=\text{kg}\). The cubic metres cancel, leaving kilograms. Thus \(2\times 5=10\), so the mass is \(10\text{ kg}\). Option B incorrectly keeps the density unit.
questions.hint: Keep track of whether the physical formula requires multiplication or division.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate distance by multiplying speed in \(\text{km/h}\) by time in hours.
questions.question: A train travels at \(72\text{ km/h}\) for \(2\text{ h}\). What distance does it cover, with units simplified?
questions.explanation: Speed multiplied by time gives distance: \(\frac{\text{km}}{\text{h}}\times \text{h}=\text{km}\). The hours cancel, leaving kilometres. Since \(72\times 2=144\), the distance is \(144\text{ km}\). Option B incorrectly leaves the speed unit.
questions.hint: Write the units beside every factor before simplifying.

questions.learningObjective: Identify which expression simplifies to the unit of speed.
questions.question: Which expression simplifies to \(\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}}\)?
questions.explanation: Multiplying acceleration by time gives \(\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}^2}\times \text{s}=\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}}\). One factor of seconds cancels. Option A divides by seconds again, giving \(\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}^3}\), not speed.
questions.hint: Cancel only matching units in a numerator and denominator.

questions.learningObjective: Combine physical units correctly in a force-area quotient.
questions.question: A force of \(100\text{ N}\) acts uniformly over an area of \(4\text{ m}^2\). What is the pressure, with units simplified?
questions.explanation: Pressure is force divided by area, so \(\frac{100}{4}=25\) with quotient unit \(\text{N/m}^2\). The alternative divides the numerical values but multiplies their units, giving \(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2\), which is not pressure.
questions.hint: Keep track of whether the physical formula requires multiplication or division.

questions.learningObjective: Combine physical units correctly in a power-time product.
questions.question: A device of power \(50\text{ W}\) operates for \(10\text{ s}\). What is the energy transferred, with units simplified?
questions.explanation: Energy equals power multiplied by time: \(\text{W}\times\text{s}=\text{W}\cdot\text{s}\), which is the joule. Therefore, \(50\times 10=500\), so the energy is \(500\text{ W}\cdot\text{s}\). Option A incorrectly divides power by time.
questions.hint: Write the units beside every factor before simplifying.

questions.learningObjective: Combine physical units correctly in a product of derived quantities.
questions.question: The expression \(\left(\text{kg}\cdot\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}^2}\right)\times \text{m}\) simplifies to which unit?
questions.explanation: Multiplying the unit of force by metres gives \(\left(\text{kg}\cdot\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}^2}\right)\times\text{m}=\frac{\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2}{\text{s}^2}\). This is the unit of energy, the joule. Option A omits the extra metre.
questions.hint: Multiply the unit symbols factor by factor and collect repeated units as powers.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the spring constant with correctly simplified units.
questions.question: A spring obeys \(F=kx\). If \(F=30\text{ N}\) and \(x=0.5\text{ m}\), what is \(k\) with units simplified?
questions.explanation: Rearranging Hooke's law gives \(k=\frac{F}{x}\). Therefore, the unit of \(k\) is \(\text{N/m}\). Then \(\frac{30}{0.5}=60\), so \(k=60\text{ N/m}\). Option B incorrectly multiplies force by extension.
questions.hint: Keep track of whether the physical formula requires multiplication or division.

questions.learningObjective: Identify a calculation in which identical units cancel completely.
questions.question: Which calculation produces a result with no unit, that is, a dimensionless ratio?
questions.explanation: In \(\frac{10\text{ m}}{5\text{ m}}\), the metre units cancel completely, leaving the dimensionless number \(2\). Option B multiplies metres by metres and produces square metres, so it is not dimensionless.
questions.hint: Write the units beside every factor before simplifying.
